body.text: 10. Strategic Compliance Checklist for Canadian Claimants (2026–2027)

To maximize cash recoveries and insulate claims against CRA audit adjustments under the post-Bill C-15 and Budget 2026 rules, corporate tax directors and R&D leaders should execute the following eight-point compliance protocol:

items: Apply the $6 Million Expenditure Limit and Evaluate the Gross Revenue Phase-Out Election: Ensure all corporate tax provision workpapers and Schedule T2SCH31 / T2SCH49 calculations for taxation years beginning after December 15, 2024 apply the $6,000,000 expenditure limit and $15M–$75M phase-out range (including on Form T666 for British Columbia claims). If a CCPC has raised venture equity or debt that pushes its prior-year taxable capital above $15 million while its 3-year average gross revenue remains below $15 million, formally elect the 3-year average gross revenue phase-out method to preserve the full $2.1 million refundable federal credit.

Screen Public Companies for ECPC Qualification: Canadian-resident public companies listed on a designated stock exchange (and their 90%+ owned Canadian subsidiaries) that are not controlled by non-residents should model their 3-year average gross revenue. If average gross revenue is below $75 million, transition from non-refundable 15% ITC planning to claiming the 35% enhanced refundable ITC as an Eligible Canadian Public Corporation (ECPC).

Capture Post-December 15, 2024 Capital Equipment, SUE, and Leases: Track operating time logs for all lab machinery, prototyping equipment, testing rigs, and compute hardware acquired or leased after December 15, 2024. Report assets used ≥90% (ASA) in SR&ED on Lines 262–263, Line 390, and Box 780 of Form T661; report new dual-use equipment used >50% to <90% in SR&ED (and not excluded as PDP under Regulation 2900(11)) as First-Term and Second-Term SUE (25% per term) on Line 504 and Box 792; and claim eligible equipment leases on Lines 350, 355, or 360.

Structure Specified Employee Compensation Around Regular Payroll, Not Year-End Bonuses or Dividends: Because subsection 37(9) disqualifies bonuses and profit-based remuneration for specified employees (10%+ shareholders and non-arm's length relatives) and dividends earn $0 in SR&ED credits, pay technical founders via regular periodic T4 salary up to the 5 × YMPE cap ($373,000 in 2026) (noting that the 55% proxy base maxes out at the lesser of 75% of salary or 2.5 × YMPE [$186,500 in 2026]). Ensure all accrued wages and current SR&ED expenses are physically paid within 180 days of taxation year-end under subsections 78(4) and 127(26).

Model the Traditional vs. Proxy Method Trade-Off Before Filing Form T661: Because the election on Lines 160–162 of Form T661 is irrevocable once filed, model both methods whenever incremental cloud computing (AWS/GCP GPU clusters), shop-floor utilities, and non-direct support salaries exceed 55% of the capped proxy salary base.

Transition Québec Operations to the New CRIC Regime (Form RD-1029.8.CR-T): For taxation years beginning after March 25, 2025, expand Québec project tracking beyond traditional SR&ED to capture pre-commercialization regulatory validation/certification testing and product design (form, aesthetics, functionality, materials) on Form RD-1029.8.PR and Form RD-1029.8.CR-T to claim the 30% refundable CRIC on the first $1 million above the exclusion threshold and 20% refundable on the excess.

Frame Technical Narratives Around System-Level Technological Uncertainties, Never Cost Targets: Following 6398316 Canada Inc. (2021 TCC 17), Dazzm Inc. (2024 TCC 129), and Willowglen Systems (2026 TCC 7), ensure Part 2 narratives on Form T661 articulate the underlying scientific or system-level technological constraints, the specific hypotheses formulated, and the empirical metrics recorded during testing—never framing the uncertainty around commercial cost targets or routine software modernization. Maintain contemporaneous project records and time-tracking logs for the full 6-year statutory retention period under paragraph 230(4)(b).

Leverage the CRA Elective Pre-Claim Approval Process for High-Value Projects: For multi-year R&D initiatives where cash-flow timing is critical, submit an optional Pre-Claim Approval application (up to 3 projects, valid for up to 3 years) prior to commencing work to obtain an RTA eligibility determination within 8 weeks and qualify for the accelerated 90-day post-filing expenditure review standard.
